5967.t: From περιφερής (peripherḗs, “circular; rounded; revolving; wavering”) + -ια (-ia), from περιφέρω (periphérō, “to carry round; revolve; wander”), from περι- (peri-, “around, surrounding”) + φέρω (phérō, “to carry, bear”) from Proto-Hellenic *pʰérō (“to…

5985.t: From Proto-Hellenic *plékō, from Proto-Indo-European *pleḱ-. Cognate with Latin plectō (“to plait, weave, twist”).

5987.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *plew- Proto-Indo-European *-mṓ Proto-Indo-European *pléwmō Ancient Greek πλεύμων (pleúmōn) ▲ Ancient Greek πνέω (pnéō)influ. ▲ Ancient Greek πνεῦμα (pneûma)influ.

5944.t: From παροξύνω (paroxúnō, “to sharpen, irritate”) + -μός (-mós), from παρά (pará, “beside”) + ὀξύνω (oxúnō, “to sharpen”).

5900.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ksuyō, from Proto-Indo-European *ksuyéti, from *ksew- (“to scrape, shave, scratch”). Cognate with Latin novācula, saucius, and many others.

5908.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁eys-, used to form words denoting passion; see also Latin īra (“anger”), Lithuanian aistra (“violent passion”), Avestan 𐬀𐬉𐬴𐬨𐬀 (aēṣ̌ma, “anger”).

5912.t: From οὐρέω (ouréō, “to urinate”). Not related to Latin ūrīna.

5984.t: Traditionally derived from πλατύς (plătŭ́s, “broad; flat”), or taken to be inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥th₂enós (“wide; broad”), under the assumption that the tree was named after its broad leaves or flat patches of bark.

5911.t: From οὖσα (oûsă, feminine present participle of εἰμί (eimĭ́, “to be”)) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix). Literally, “beingness”.

5915.t: From a petrified case form of Proto-Indo-European *per- (“beyond, across”), originally meaning "other side"; compare πέραν (pérān, “across”).

5954.t: From περί (perí). Compare περικαλλής (perikallḗs, “very beautiful”), Latin permagnus (“very great”) etc.

5988.t: No clear etymology. Earlier attempts to analyze the formation as a conflation of several different verbs are unconvincing.

5979.t: The etymological base of the word is not clear. Formally, there is no reason to disconnect the word from πλάσσω (plássō, “to knead, mold”), but this linkage is not evident on the semantic side.

5904.t: From οἶνος (oînos, “wine”) + χοή (khoḗ, “act of pouring”, also “libation (to the dead)”), from the root of χέω (khéō, “to pour”).

5950.t: Derived from πέλεκυς (pélekus, “axe”), because of the functional and/or formal similarity with an axe.

5982.t: Verbal adjective, from πλώω (plṓō, “to sail, float”) + -τός (-tós).

5978.t: A conflation of πιέζω (piézō, “squeeze”) and βιάζομαι (biázomai, “force”).
